correctness.rationale: For \(n=2pq\), the equation is exactly \(d_1-d_2=-pq+3p+3q+3\). The proof splits on the smaller odd prime. For \(p=3,5,7\), divisor types reduce to finite equations in coefficients from \(\{1,2,p,2p\}\), with all solutions listed. For \(p\ge11\), the required magnitude exceeds every difference of two non-\(q\) divisors; two \(q\)-multiples are excluded modulo \(q\); and the remaining mixed case yields inequalities impossible for \(t=1,2\). Each of the eight witnesses is checked directly. The packaged verifier independently reconstructs the finite reductions and performs a regression scan.
